title: Gambling Dealers
description: Operate table games. Stand or sit behind table and operate games of chance by dispensing the appropriate number of cards or blocks to players, or operating other gambling equipment. Distribute winnings or collect players' money or chips. May compare the house's hand against players' hands.

clusters.label: Performing for or Working Directly with the Public

tasks.text: Check to ensure that all players have placed bets before play begins.
Deal cards to house hands, and compare these with players' hands to determine winners, as in black jack.
Stand behind a gaming table and deal the appropriate number of cards to each player.
Apply rule variations to card games such as poker, in which players bet on the value of their hands.
Conduct gambling games, such as dice, roulette, cards, or keno, following all applicable rules and regulations.
Work as part of a team of dealers in games, such as baccarat or craps.
Start and control games and gaming equipment, and announce winning numbers or colors.
Open and close cash floats and game tables.
Answer questions about game rules and casino policies.
Participate in games for gambling establishments to provide the minimum complement of players at a table.
Pay winnings or collect losing bets as established by the rules and procedures of a specific game.
Exchange paper currency for playing chips or coin money.
Receive, verify, and record patrons' cash wagers.
Prepare collection reports for submission to supervisors.
Greet customers and make them feel welcome.
Refer patrons to gaming cashiers to collect winnings.
Inspect cards and equipment to be used in games to ensure that they are in good condition.
Supervise staff and monitor gambling tables to ensure security of the game.

clusters.label: Estimating the Quantifiable Characteristics of Products, Events, or Information

tasks.text: Compute amounts of players' wins or losses, or scan winning tickets presented by patrons to calculate the amount of money won.
Seat patrons at gaming tables.
Train new dealers.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Data base management system software
skills.def: Software to store, organize, or provide access to a set of related information. Examples: Apache Hadoop.

skills.name: Business intelligence and data analysis software
skills.def: Software to present, visualize, or analyze data to help businesses make informed decisions. Examples: Apache Spark.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Cloud-based data access and sharing software
skills.def: Software to share or co-author computer files through cloud computing, where documents are stored in a central "cloud" of networked servers. Examples: Slack.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Email software.
